sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 46.6% a year from $6.91 billion in FY2017 to $215.9 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F211].
The path was not smooth: revenue fell 6.8% in FY2020 and was flat in FY2023 before jumping 125.9% in FY2024 and 114.2% in FY2025 [D130][D284][D338][D393].
The FY2024 step change came from Data Center revenue up 217% on Hopper shipments for LLM training and inference [P22][P23].
FY2026 growth of 65.5% was again data center compute and networking, with Blackwell the majority of Data Center revenue [D448][P10].
Data Center was 89.7% of FY2026 revenue and contributed 60.2pp of the 65.5% growth [D620][D622][D448].
Within it, Data Center computing grew 59% on Blackwell demand and networking grew 142% on NVLink for GB200 and GB300 systems [P8].
Networking contributed 14.1pp of FY2026 growth, up from 7.2pp in FY2025 [D636][D633].
Operating income grew 60.1% against revenue growth of 65.5%, an incremental margin of 57.3% [D449][D448][D475].
Diluted EPS grew 66.7% versus net income growth of 64.7%, helped by a 1.2% lower diluted share count [D452][D450][D470].
Operating margin was 60.4% in FY2026, against a window median of 32.8%, a high of 62.4% in FY2025 and a low of 15.7% in FY2023 [F50][D813][D812][D811].
The FY2026 margin fell 2.0pp as cost of revenue took off 3.9pp, partly offset by R&D and SG&A adding 1.3pp and 0.6pp [D463][D477][D478][D479].
The cost-of-revenue drag includes a $4.5 billion H20 excess inventory and purchase obligation charge in the first quarter [P7].
R&D rose 43.2% on a 29% increase in compensation and a 79% increase in compute and infrastructure [D466][P5].

Net margin of 55.6% sits 4.8pp below operating margin, with other income of $11.1 billion partly offsetting a 15.1% tax rate [F70][D861][X120][D434]; the filing attributes the other income to unrealized gains on equity securities [P3].
Operating cash flow of $102.7 billion was 0.86x net income, the window low against a 0.97x median [F100][F60][D435][D851].
Free cash flow of $96.7 billion was a 44.8% margin, just below the 46.6% FY2025 high [F110][D432][D821].
Capex of $6.04 billion was 2.8% of revenue and 2.13x D&A, up from 1.74x in FY2025 [F105][F10][D431][D437][D382].
Inventory grew 112.3% and receivables 66.8%, both faster than revenue, lifting days inventory to 125 and DSO to 65 [D474][D473][D446][D445].
Cash and investments of $43.2 billion against $8.47 billion of debt left net cash of $34.7 billion at FY2025 [D384][D440][D386].
That FY2026 net-cash figure omits short-term investments, which were not reported that year, so the liquidity comparison across the gap is incomplete [R3].
Return on average equity was 101.5%, against a semis peer median of 20.3% (n=6) [D447][D849].
Buybacks and dividends of $41.1 billion absorbed 42.5% of free cash flow, and the share count fell 1.2% [D443][D444][D470].
Short-term investments were not reported in FY2026 after $34.6 billion in FY2025, so net cash and its peer rank for that year are understated [R3][X188].
Customer concentration is high: one direct customer was 22% of FY2026 revenue and another 14%, both mainly Compute & Networking [P6].
China revenue fell 21.4% in FY2026 and its share dropped to 9.1% from 19.2%, a 4.1pp drag on growth [D545][D544][D541][D546].
The Graphics segment fell 25.0% in FY2023 when it was 44.1% of revenue, showing how concentrated the model was before Data Center took over [R1][D754][D753].
Operating margin: a print below the FY2025 high of 62.4% would extend the FY2026 compression, while a recovery above it would reverse it [D812][F50].
Cash conversion: operating cash flow below 0.86x net income would mark a new window low versus the 0.97x median [D435][D851].
Inventory: days inventory above the FY2026 level of 125 would signal further build against the 113 days of FY2025 [D446][D391].
